comparison: Both evaluate experimental design and data collection procedures (C1-C2, C28-C39) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes methodological details (C145-C155) which peer review addresses separately in R17. Both find the experimental setup sound and well-documented.

OpenEval R1 includes methodological claims C145-C155 which peer review evaluates separately in R17. Both find methods sound and carefully executed. Peer review R17 focuses specifically on methodological rigor while OpenEval R1 combines experimental design with methods.

Both evaluate behavioral findings on trials attempted/succeeded and movement vigor (C3-C4, C58-C61, C64-C65, C108) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical details (p<10^-24 to p<10^-50), while peer review confirms findings align with qualitative model predictions. Strong agreement on core behavioral results.

OpenEval R4 addresses saccade and lick vigor reductions with tube distance (C4, C21, C64-C65, C79-C80, C109). Peer R2 confirms these findings align with model predictions. Both find evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests.

Both evaluate the counterintuitive vigor-accuracy relationship for saccades (C62-C63, C66-C67, C110) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistics (F>250, p<10^-50), peer review accepts findings without criticism. Both note this challenges typical speed-accuracy tradeoff.

Both evaluate lick vigor characterization (C74-C78, C84) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistics and temporal dynamics, peer review confirms analyses were carefully executed. Strong agreement on lick vigor findings.

Both evaluate reward accumulation effects on lick vigor (C87-C88, C96, C112) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval reports strong statistics (F=152-353, p<10^-50), peer review confirms results are robust. Agreement on reward modulation of vigor.

Both evaluate trial-by-trial reward effects on vigor (C89-C93, C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed t-tests showing differential effects between successful and failed licks, peer review confirms findings are robust without criticism.

Both evaluate pupil-vigor coordination across movement types (C5, C7, C9, C22-C25, C70-C73, C81-C86, C116-C120) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes temporal correspondence and statistical significance, peer review describes this as 'solid pupillometric evidence.' Strong agreement on pupil findings.

Both evaluate strong correlations between pupil size and vigor (C24, C103-C106) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval reports very high correlations (r=0.97-0.99), peer review describes this as solid evidence for coordination. Agreement on generality across movement types.

Both evaluate hunger/weight effects (C99-C102, C111) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes partial support with dissociation between lick and saccade vigor, peer review confirms quasi-experimental increases in reward value led to predicted effects. Both accept the findings despite incomplete alignment with predictions.

Both evaluate authors' acknowledgment of discrepancies (C113-C114) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this honest reporting strengthens credibility, peer review accepts that not all predictions were confirmed. Agreement that limitations were appropriately acknowledged.

Both evaluate subject-specific differences in lick vigor-accuracy relationship (C94-C95) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as an important limitation, peer review accepts data as presented without criticism. Agreement on reporting of individual differences.

Both evaluate LC-NE mechanistic interpretation (C26-C27, C121-C127) but differ in evaluation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting speculation requires direct neural validation, peer review rates as SUPPORTED accepting pupil-indexed brain state interpretation. Disagreement on certainty level of mechanistic claims.

Both evaluate dopamine/basal ganglia mechanistic proposals (C128-C137) but differ in evaluation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting these are informed speculation not directly tested, peer review rates as SUPPORTED accepting discussion-level interpretations. Disagreement on certainty of mechanistic hypotheses.

Both evaluate NE/cerebellum mechanisms for vigor-accuracy relationship (C138-C144) but differ in evaluation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring direct neural testing, peer review rates as SUPPORTED accepting discussion-level proposals. Disagreement on certainty of mechanistic explanations.

Both evaluate theoretical foundation and foraging theory framework (C12-C17, C107) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and well-established framework, peer review describes model as interesting and comprehensive. Strong agreement on theoretical grounding.

OpenEval R2 evaluates mathematical formulations and model predictions (C40-C41, C43, C46-C47, C53-C57) as SUPPORTED. Peer R15 evaluates overlapping theoretical framework claims (C40-C41, C43, C46-C47, C107) also as SUPPORTED. Both find the theoretical model well-grounded and predictions clearly stated.

OpenEval R2 includes model predictions about coordinated effects (C53-C57), peer R5 evaluates overlapping predictions (C18, C20, C53-C57, C98) as SUPPORTED. Both agree the model makes testable predictions about decisions and movements, though peer review groups with broader prediction claims.

OpenEval R18 evaluates bridge between theory and experiment (C18-C21) as SUPPORTED, peer R5 evaluates overlapping theoretical predictions (C18, C20, C53-C57, C98) as SUPPORTED. Both confirm key qualitative predictions were met.
OpenEval R18 includes confirmation that subjects stockpiled food (C19), peer R4 evaluates this claim as SUPPORTED. Both agree on this behavioral finding aligning with model predictions.
OpenEval R3 includes temporal consistency finding (C60), peer R4 evaluates this as SUPPORTED. Both accept the finding that monkeys collect more food before consumption when effort increases.

Peer review R18 evaluates citation to prior work (C115) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval does not separately evaluate this citation, which appears in context of acknowledging discrepancies (OpenEval R12 mentions C115 in evaluation text but not in claim_ids).

Peer review R19 evaluates pupil size literature foundation (C68-C69) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval does not separately evaluate these claims, which provide background for pupil measurements used throughout the study.
